ety.text: From Middle English leopard, leopart, lepard, leperd, from Old French leopard (“leopard”), from Late Latin leopardus (“leopon, lipard”) from late Ancient Greek λεόπαρδος (leópardos, “leopon, lipard”), from λέων (léōn, “lion”) + πάρδος (párdos, “pard, male leopard”), from earlier πάρδαλις (párdalis, “leopard”), probably from an unattested Old Persian [Term?] term ancestral to Middle Persian [script needed] (palang), Khwarezmian [script needed] (plyk), Sogdian [script needed] (pwrδnk), Pashto پړانګ (pṛāng). Compare Persian پلنگ (palang) and Sanskrit पृदाकु (pṛdāku, “panther”).

senses.d: A large wild cat with a spotted coat native to Africa and Asia (Panthera pardus).
ex: Leopard skins have always been desirable commodities because of their spectacular spotted patterns.

The snow leopard (Panthera uncia), a large wild cat native to Asia.
Any of various nymphalid butterflies of the genus Phalanta, having black markings on an orange base.
